original_question: For the Aztec window obtained by deleting a centered Aztec diamond of order x from an outer Aztec diamond of order y, find a general formula for the number of domino tilings. In particular, explain the observed polynomial dependence on x when y=x+w for fixed even w.
target_in_paper: Section 3 ("Dominoes"), Problem 14: "Find a general formula for the number of domino tilings of Aztec windows."
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the same region as the paper: an Aztec window formed by deleting a centered inner Aztec diamond of order x from an outer Aztec diamond of order y. It also captures the paper’s main goal—an explicit counting formula for domino tilings—and it picks up the nearby special-case phenomenon emphasized in the text, namely the polynomial dependence on x when y = x + w with w fixed and even.
missing_details: Use the paper’s terminology explicitly: the region is called the Aztec window, with outer order y and inner order x.
State that x and y are integer orders, with 0 <= x < y.
The official problem is broader than the fixed-gap subfamily y = x + w: it asks for a formula for all Aztec windows.
If the fixed-gap subfamily is singled out, quantify it as: for each fixed even integer w, with y = x + w.
Include the parity obstruction stated in the nearby context: when w is odd and x is large enough, the Aztec window has no domino tilings.
Clarify that the polynomial-in-x statement is part of the motivating context around the problem, not the exact wording of Problem 14 itself.

The nearby discussion also records an additional empirical functional-composition factorization pattern for these polynomials; your draft omits this contextual feature, though it is not part of the official statement.

No ambient field/ring, homogeneity condition, degree restriction, nilpotency hypothesis, or operator definition is involved here; the parameters are integer lattice orders and the output is an integer tiling count.
refined_question: Let W_{x,y} denote the Aztec window obtained by deleting from the center of the Aztec diamond of order y the concentric Aztec diamond of order x, where x and y are integers with 0 <= x < y. Determine a general formula for the number T(W_{x,y}) of tilings of W_{x,y} by 1x2 and 2x1 dominos. In particular, for each fixed even integer w, determine explicitly the polynomial in x giving T(W_{x,x+w}), and incorporate the parity obstruction noted in the paper that when w is odd and x is large enough, W_{x,x+w} has no domino tilings.
justification: The draft is aiming at the Aztec-window problem in Section 3. The paper first defines the Aztec window and then discusses the special regime y = x + w, noting on pages 23-25 that for fixed even w the tiling count appears polynomial in x, while for odd w and x large enough there are no tilings; it also records the observed composition-factorization pattern of these polynomials. Immediately after that context, Problem 14 on page 25 asks, in the paper’s official formulation, for a general formula for the number of domino tilings of Aztec windows. The refined question therefore keeps the full scope of Problem 14 while adding the integer-order, centering, and parity details needed to make it stand alone. There is no explicit equivalent reformulation proved in the paper; the only nearby sharpening is the progress note on page 25 saying that, for each fixed w, transfer-matrix methods show the count is polynomial in x.
